newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN RUPIAH RECOVERS IN LATE TRADING.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN RUPIAH RECOVERS IN LATE TRADING.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah recovered against the dollar in late trading on Thursday after being hit earlier by a sharp decline in the stock market, dealers said.
They said the rupiah bounced back to 2,589/94 at 0900 GMT from a low of 2,600 but was off its early high of 2,582.0. The rupiah opened at 2,586.0/91.0 on Thursday.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,587.5/90.5 and 2,581.5/83.5, respectively.
Dealers said the stock market plunge spilled over to the currency market, triggering short dollar buying and profit-taking in thin midday trading.
But they said local operators initiated fresh rupiah buying which was followed by some foreign players, helping the currency recover although it was still off its early high.
The rupiah was on the road to recovery in the morning and was attempting to break the 2,580 resistance level before the stock market's plunge stopped its advance.

Operators had gone short on dollars earlier as confidence in the rupiah returned following a central bank meeting with foreign bankers on Wednesday at which no mention was made of foreign exchange controls.
The stock markets's composite index made its second steepest fall on record after the 33.54 point dive last year in the aftermath of the July 27 Jakarta riots.
The index dropped 26.14 points to 673.72 before closing at 677.94, down 21.92 points, or 3.13 percent, on Thursday.
Stock brokers said the plunge was due to new margin rules from the Capital Market Supervisory Agency (Bapepam) which forced investors to cut their holdings.
"This seems to have caused heavy unloading and triggered further liquidation as many of them could not meet margin calls," one major local broker said.
Among the new rules, Bapepam required margin investors to provide a deposit of at least 50 percent of the value of share purchases. Previously, margins could be as high as one-for-five.
Brokers said they were also forcing investors to cut their holdings to meet Bapepam's requirements in order to obtain a margin licence from the authority.
They said offshore selling in selective big-capitalised companies added to the woes of new rules and margin calls.
Analysts said some earnings were also revisited following the recent sharp decline of the rupiah against the dollar.
Currency dealers said swaps were softer following an easing of short-term money rates in the interbank market although the central bank maintained relatively high short-term rates.
Overnight money fell to 14.25 percent from 18.0 percent, driving longer-term rates lower across the board.
The central bank kept its interest rates for short-term bilateral papers (SBIs) unchanged on Thursday and remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market.

The bank offered overnight bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, four-to-six day at 15.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
Economists said the high short-term rates were temporary and subject to revision once the currency market stabilised.
Overnight swap was at 0.55/0.60 and tom/next at 1.4/1.5.
One-month swap was at 17.0/20.0, two at 39.0/43.0, three at 57.0/63.0 and six at 116.0/125.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,567/2,615 on Thursday from 2,572/2,620 on Wednesday.
